chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim from Ali (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a Muslim man whom illness or some matter for which God excuses him prevents from performing Hajj. He said: 'He must send a substitute to perform Hajj on his behalf from his wealth, if he has no wealth [to perform it himself].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muslim who cannot perform Hajj due to illness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (AS) clarifies the ruling for a Muslim unable to perform Hajj due to illness or valid excuse, mandating that they send a proxy to perform Hajj on their behalf using their wealth. This establishes the principle of *Hajj al-Badal* (substitute Hajj), emphasizing that financial capacity remains the key condition even when physical presence is impeded. The ruling underscores the enduring obligation of Hajj as a debt to God that must be fulfilled either personally or through representation.
